---

This chapter introduces the Julia structures needed to turn a conceptual behavioral rule into an executable mechanism.

## Planned learning outcomes

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. Define and call a Julia function.
2. Read multiline and abbreviated function definitions.
3. Distinguish positional arguments from keyword arguments.
4. Explain how a Julia function determines its returned value.
5. Use `if`, `elseif`, and `else` to express a decision.
6. Use a `for` loop to repeat an action.
7. Combine comparisons and Boolean operators into a condition.
8. Modify a mutable collection and interpret the `!` naming convention.
9. Generate random values with an explicitly supplied random-number generator.
10. Inspect a developing rule with `println`, `@show`, `typeof`, and small checks.
11. Build and explain a miniature time-step simulation using Julia vectors and functions.

## Planned scope

The simulated population will be represented by a Boolean vector. `true` means that an individual has adopted a practice and `false` means that the individual has not. During each step, one individual observes another and may adopt. A loop repeats the rule and records the number of adopters.

The chapter remains in ordinary Julia rather than Agents.jl. Its pedagogical purpose is to make the mechanism understandable before a framework organizes it.

## Culminating activity

The learner will predict the effect of a behavioral rule, run the vector-based simulation, inspect the adoption count over time, and explain which lines represent state, interaction, chance, and change.
